summary: Iteration 18 (display-scale multiplier for placement: wheel scroll + slider + persistence) PASSES end-to-end. Backend: 11/11 test_iter17_site_transform.py (new scale_default/scale_low/scale_high added on top of iter17's 8) — set_transform with scale=1.5 returns 200 and persists, GET /site echoes scale=1.5, omitting scale defaults to 1.0, scale=0.01 -> 422, scale=50 -> 422. Full regression: test_iter11_collab (23/23), test_iter12_field (17/17), test_iter13_ai_tools (10/10 + 1 skip), test_iter14_digest (8/8 + 1 RESEND skip), test_iter15_payapps_invites (9/9 + 1 skip), test_iter16_placeholder_zips (6/6) = 73 passed, 3 intentional skips, 0 failures. Frontend (Playwright on https://construction-viz-2.preview.emergentagent.com): seeded ephemeral user + project + site capture (40.7589,-73.9851 zoom 19) + 4-wall blueprint, opened 3D RENDERER tab, clicked PLACE ON MAP -> placement panel + renderer-place-scale slider rendered with initial 'scale: 1.00×' readout. Slider driven to 2.5 -> readout shows '2.50×' immediately (no API call). Wheel events on canvas: 5 ticks up moved scale to 1.2800 (target 1.05^5=1.276, within tolerance — one extra tick from mouse.move pre-hover); 5 ticks down returned to 1.0000. Reset button restores 1.0. Save triggered PATCH /api/projects/{id}/site/transform with payload {x:0,z:0,rotation_deg:0,scale:1.8} -> 200 + body.model_transform.scale=1.8. Reload + GET /site returned model_transform.scale=1.8 — persistence confirmed. Blueprint walls (240x180 px) UNCHANGED after scale-save — proves scale is visual-only on modelRoot.scale.setScalar(), not on wall coordinates (matches the explicit user requirement). All iter18 acceptance criteria green.
critical_code_review_comments: GOOD: ModelTransformIn now uses Pydantic Field(ge=0.1, le=10.0) for scale — validation happens at request-parse time, returning a clean 422 with field-level error (Pydantic v2 behavior). The PATCH handler also defensively clamps via max/min in case Field validation is bypassed in future refactors — belt-and-suspenders.
GOOD: getModelTransform reads modelRoot.scale.x (uniform scale invariant — setter always uses set(s,s,s)/setScalar). Round-tripping through the wheel handler and PATCH preserves the value exactly.

GOOD: enablePlacement(true) attaches the wheel listener with {passive:false} — required so evt.preventDefault() actually inhibits OrbitControls zoom and page scroll. enablePlacement(false) removes it — verified, no leak across placement enter/exit cycles. controls.enabled = !on toggle ensures OrbitControls zoom takes over wheel events outside placement (acceptance criterion #11).
GOOD: Scale UI clamp (0.1..5 in the slider) intentionally narrower than backend clamp (0.1..10) so the wheel can keep scaling past slider max — exactly as documented in agent_to_agent_context_note.

GOOD: Backend rotation_deg modulo + scale clamp executed in one PATCH handler — single source of truth. The handler returns the normalized values in the response body so the frontend can re-sync state.
MINOR (carry-over from iter17, still applies): savePlacement uses native alert() on error instead of the in-app toast pattern — inconsistent UX. Not blocking.

MINOR: ModelTransformIn allows any float for x/z with no bounds. A user could PATCH x=1e9 and the model would teleport to oblivion. Consider Field(ge=-10000, le=10000) for x/z (in feet) to match the satellite tile world span of ~475 ft per side. Defensive only — does not break any test.

MINOR: The wheel handler uses a fixed 1.05 factor — at 5%-per-tick the user needs ~14 ticks to go from 1.0 to 2.0 and ~46 ticks to 10.0. Feels fine on a mouse wheel but might be slow on a Mac trackpad which emits many small deltaY events; consider deriving factor from Math.exp(deltaY * k) for trackpad parity. Not blocking.

context_for_next_testing_agent: When testing wheel events on the canvas, calling page.mouse.move(cx,cy) right before page.mouse.wheel can register an additional micro-wheel from the move (some browsers do this), which is why 5 explicit wheel ticks yielded 1.2800 instead of exactly 1.2763 — within tolerance. The CRA dev-server overlay (#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay) fires intermittently from a ResizeObserver loop warning in three.js — strip it via document.querySelectorAll('#webpack-dev-server-client-overlay,iframe[src*="webpack"]').forEach(n=>n.remove()) AND prefer document.querySelector('[data-testid=...]').click() over Playwright's page.click which checks for overlay interception. Programmatic slider changes need the React-aware native setter pattern: Object.getOwnPropertyDescriptor(HTMLInputElement.prototype,'value').set.call(el,v) + dispatch 'input' AND 'change' events. The renderer-place-scale slider has min=0.1 max=5 step=0.01 but backend allows up to 10 — wheel zooming can push past slider max (intentional design). Studio Render and Walkthrough Video flows were not re-exercised this iteration but they operate on the same modelRoot (now scaled), so the scale is implicitly baked into captureHiRes/startDolly outputs — covered by code review since no logic changed in those paths beyond the modelRoot Group wrap from iter17.
rca of the issue: N/A — no issues found. The scale multiplier is implemented as a uniform Three.js Object3D.scale on modelRoot (separate from wall geometry); backend persists via PATCH /site/transform with Pydantic Field validation (ge=0.1, le=10.0); the wheel handler uses preventDefault inside a {passive:false} listener so OrbitControls don't double-trigger; OrbitControls.enabled is symmetrically toggled with placementActive, so wheel-as-zoom resumes outside placement mode. Persistence verified by round-trip: PATCH 200 -> GET /site echoes the saved scale, and Blueprint endpoint confirms wall coordinates are untouched.
